title: Company-wide policies and processes
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel policy, and canonical internal templates. Its purpose is to standardize decision-making, reduce risk, and provide a single reference for approvals, owners, and cadence.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors accessing Redwood systems or acting on behalf of Redwood.
- Covers production and non-production systems, corporate data, procurement processes, vendor onboarding, and business travel booked or reimbursed by Redwood.

Primary owners and escalation contacts:
- People Ops (policy owner, policy lifecycle): Maya Chen <maya@redwood.ai>
- Security & Compliance (access and data controls): Diego Ramirez <diego@redwood.ai>
- Finance & Legal (procurement, vendor contracts, expenses): Priya Nair <priya@redwood.ai>
- Engineering (technical change management): Liam O'Connor <liam@redwood.ai>

1) Access & Permissions
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access, timely onboarding/offboarding, and documented privileged access.
Key policies:
- Principle: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) enforced across core services (GCP/AWS, GitHub, Okta, Snowflake, internal services).
- Onboarding: People Ops creates initial accounts; team leads request service access via access-request form (internal template link below). Requests must list business justification and required duration.
- Offboarding: People Ops must submit termination in HRIS within 2 business hours of notice. Automated deprovisioning runs nightly; for high-risk roles (SRE, infra, security) manual deprovisioning must be completed within 4 hours.
- Privileged access: Any user requiring admin/privileged access must have a documented justification, an owner, and a 90-day review cadence. Emergency privileged access must be requested through the Just-In-Time (JIT) portal and logged in the privileged-access audit table.
- Access reviews: Owners run quarterly access reviews per system. Findings and remediation steps are tracked in the Access Review tracker.
Approval flow:
1) Team lead submits access-request using the Access Request template.
2) System owner (usually infra/security) reviews; if approved, change ticket is created and Okta group membership updated.
3) People Ops verifies onboarding/offboarding tasks are complete.

2) Change Management (Technical & Non-Technical)
Purpose: Minimize disruption to production, ensure visibility and fast rollback. Applies to infra, runtime, config, and product-facing changes.
Definitions:
- Standard change: low-risk, pre-approved changes (minor config tweaks) that do not require CAB review.
- Significant change: changes that affect latency, reliability, data retention, or security posture; require CAB review and a rollout plan.
- Emergency change: unplanned remediation to restore service. Post-facto CAB review required within 72 hours.
Process (Significant change):
1) Create a Jira change ticket with impact analysis, rollback plan, scheduling window, and runbook.
2) Submit Change Request to the Change Advisory Board (CAB) at least 5 business days before the planned window. Attach test results and canary metrics.
3) CAB decision: approve / request revisions / reject.
4) On approval, schedule a canary rollout; observe metrics for the defined canary period (typically 30-60 minutes for runtime changes).
5) If canary passes, proceed to gradual rollout with monitoring and automatic rollback thresholds.
Change window guidance:
- Production: typical maintenance windows are Tue/Wed 02:00-06:00 UTC unless otherwise approved.
- High-impact changes require a blackout calendar check and customer notification (if SLA-impacting).
Emergency changes:
- Notify SRE on-call and CAB as soon as the emergency mitigates. Submit post-implementation review (PIR) within 72 hours.

3) Data Management
Purpose: Protect customer and corporate data while enabling engineering productivity.
Classification:
- Public: safe to publish.
- Internal: company-internal, non-sensitive.
- Restricted: PII, customer data, credentials, or other sensitive material.
Retention and deletion:
- Logs: short-term metrics and logs retained for 90 days by default; critical audit logs retained 7 years per compliance requirements.
- Backups: encrypted backups exist for production state; restore procedures documented in runbooks.
- Data minimization: Products should only collect minimum required fields; product teams must document retention justifications in the data register.
Encryption and keys:
- All restricted data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Key management uses the company KMS/HSM and keys rotate annually or after a suspected compromise.
Data access requests:
- Access to restricted data requires a documented business justification and approval from the data owner and Security. Temporary access is issued via the JIT portal and audited.
Data breach response:
- Follow the Security Incident Response runbook. Notify Legal and People Ops within 1 hour of confirmed compromise. Customer notification timelines are driven by severity and contract terms.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Purpose: Standardize purchasing, approvals, and expense reimbursement.
Spend tiers and approvals:
- <= $2,500: Manager approval.
- $2,500- $50,000: Department head (Finance-signed) approval and PO creation.
- > $50,000: VP/Executive approval and Legal contract review.
Process highlights:
1) Raise a purchase request in the procurement system with cost center tagging, vendor suggested, and business justification.
2) Finance validates budget availability. For capitalized purchases, Finance will classify the spend with the requestor.
3) For recurring SaaS subscriptions, use the Vendor Onboarding checklist below before signing.
Expense reimbursements:
- Employees must submit receipts within 30 days. Travel and meals follow per diem caps in the Travel section below.

5) Vendor Management and Onboarding
Purpose: Ensure vendors meet security, privacy, and contractual obligations.
Vendor classification:
- Tier 1 (Critical): vendors with access to customer data or production systems (e.g., cloud providers, monitoring, identity providers).
- Tier 2: vendors with internal data access or business-critical services.
- Tier 3: low-risk vendors (marketing platforms, office supplies).
Onboarding checklist (minimum):
- Completed Vendor Risk Assessment (security questionnaire).
- Signed Master Services Agreement (MSA) or equivalent contract reviewed by Legal.
- Insurance and SOC/ISO evidence for Tier 1.
- Data protection addenda where required by customer contracts.
- Assigned vendor owner (internal) and escalation contacts.
Vendor reviews and renewals:
- Tier 1 vendors reviewed annually; Tier 2 every 24 months; Tier 3 on renewal cycle.
- Contract renewals must be started 60 days before expiration.
Termination and offboarding:
- Remove all accounts and revoke access within the offboarding window defined in the contract. Verify data return or deletion per contract.

6) Travel Policy (Business travel and reimbursement)
Purpose: Safe, cost-effective travel that complies with regulatory and tax requirements.
Booking & approvals:
- All travel > $500 requires advance manager approval. Use the Travel Request template and preferred vendors where available.
- Class of travel: Economy for flights < 8 hours; Premium Economy/Business requires VP approval.
Per diems & expenses:
- Meals: up to $75/day domestic; $110/day international (examples - Finance maintains a country-specific table).
- Lodging: reasonable single-room rates; exceptions require pre-approval.
- Receipts: itemized receipts required for all reimbursements > $25. Use corporate cards where provided.
Safety & insurance:
- Use the company travel insurance provider for international travel; register trips with People Ops.

7) Internal Templates & Standard Forms
Canonical templates (links below):
- Access Request template (use for all non-Okta service access requests)
- Change Request template (Jira change ticket checklist)
- Vendor Onboarding checklist and Vendor Risk Assessment questionnaire
- Travel Request and Expense Reimbursement templates
- Procurement Request form and PO template
- Post-Incident Review (PIR) template and RCA checklist
Templates are stored in Confluence under /confluence/templates and must be used for auditability. Custom deviations require written approval from the policy owner.

Governance, review cadence, and exceptions
- Policy review: People Ops maintains this document and will run an annual review. Significant policy changes require cross-functional review (Security, Finance, Legal, Engineering) and CAB sign-off when changes affect operations.
- Exceptions: Temporary exceptions may be granted by the policy owner with documented mitigation and a defined expiry. Exceptions > 90 days require Executive approval.

Audit and enforcement
- Compliance evidence (access logs, vendor contracts, change tickets) must be retained according to the data retention schedule.
- Violations of these policies are handled through HR processes for employees and contract remedies for vendors. Security incidents follow the incident response playbook.

Appendix A - Quick reference table
| Area | Owner | Key artifact | Review cadence | Approval threshold |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| Access & Permissions | Security & People Ops | Access Request, Access Review tracker | quarterly | Admin access requires security approval |
| Change Management | Eng SRE | Change ticket, CAB minutes | ad-hoc / per-change | Significant changes require CAB approval |
| Data Management | Security & Product | Data register, retention policy | annual | Access to restricted data requires owner + security approval |
| Procurement & Expenses | Finance | Purchase request, PO | ongoing | > $50k requires VP + Legal review |
| Vendor Management | Finance & Legal | Vendor Risk Assessment, MSA | Tiered: 12-24 months | Tier 1 requires SOC/ISO evidence |
